placements.why: The document's content is fundamentally about instrument calibration verification — establishing that a spectrograph is calibrated and verifying it against reference standards. No existing strata category covers this organizational domain, so Calibration is minted as the home tier.
placements.title: Instrument calibration as a verifiable organizational practice
placements.frame: What counts as a completed calibration, and how is its verification established and recorded?

placements.title: Reference-plate verification settles calibration claims
placements.frame: How does verification against reference plates transform a calibration claim into trusted instrument readiness?
placements.why: Both src-1 and src-3 carry the same thematic content: calibration of the Kestrelwood spectrograph at 88.4 MHz verified against June reference plates, asserted as holding across the full observing band. src-1 performs this as Quill's expert assertion with communal 'we verified'; src-3 records it as flat cataloguing. Together they name a subject future envelopes will feed — how calibration verification against reference standards is established and recorded as settled.
